newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's National Power Corp 96 net exceeds target.
newsitem.headline: Manila's National Power Corp 96 net exceeds target.

text.p: The Philippines biggest power generation and transmission company, state-run National Power Corp (Napocor), said its net income in 1996 reached 5.542 billion pesos, up 41.6 percent from 3.914 billion in 1995.
In a statement on Wednesday, Napocor said its gross revenues amounted to 63.636 billion pesos, up 21.3 percent from 52.462 billion pesos in 1995.

"We exceeded our target by 500 million pesos for our net income and 1.28 billion pesos for our operating income. We will keep on striving for higher profitability," Napocor president Guido Delgado said.
Delgado said increased earnings of the company were due to higher energy sales, better generation mix, improved operating efficiencies and lower interest expenses.
Electricity consumption in 1996 grew by seven percent from 33,296 gigawatt-hours (GWhs) to 35,613 GWhs, he said.
Income from operations was at 13.314 billion pesos in 1996, up 15.3 percent from the previous year's 11.544 billion.
Interest expenses droppped to 6.62 billion pesos in 1996 from 7.35 billion in the previous year, he said.

The power firm's return-on-rate base (RORB) improved from 7.26 percent in 1995 to 8.25 percent last year. Under Napocor's loan covenants with creditors such as the World Bank, the firm's RORB must not be lower than eight percent.
